identity.name: Sodium propyl p-hydroxybenzoate
identity.chemical_class: Paraben preservative (p-hydroxybenzoic acid ester sodium salt)

function.mechanism: Paraben-class antimicrobial preservative that suppresses spoilage microbes (notably molds and yeasts) and extends shelf life.
common_food_categories: Direct food antimicrobial use context for related propylparaben under U.S. GMP (max 0.1%)
Synthetic flavoring substance lists (related propylparaben entry in CFR)
Historical EU proposed uses included supplements and snack-related categories

adi.basis: EFSA 2013 temporary ADI 0-10 applies only to methyl/ethyl parabens and sodium salts; E217 was not included due unresolved reproductive/developmental concerns and no clear NOAEL.

efsa.key_finding: EFSA did not support inclusion of sodium propylparaben (E217) in the temporary paraben ADI group; subsequent EU regulation removed E217 authorization.

adi.basis: ADI withdrawn in 2006 for propyl p-hydroxybenzoate; excluded from previous group ADI (0-10 mg/kg bw) due male-rat reproductive toxicity concern.

notable_bans: European Union: E217 removed from authorized Union list by Commission Regulation (EU) No 358/2014 (effective 2014-04-17).

concerns.summary: EFSA and JECFA identified reproductive/developmental uncertainty for propyl/sodium propyl parabens, including concern for male reproductive effects and lack of an adequate NOAEL for E217 inclusion in group ADI.
Recent zebrafish studies report immunotoxic and developmental toxicity signals (oxidative stress, microbiota-axis effects, craniofacial abnormalities) under experimental exposure conditions.
Recent in vitro/network study suggests procarcinogenic signaling in ER-positive breast cancer cells, but this is mechanistic preclinical evidence and not a regulatory carcinogenic classification.

no_concern_confirmed: No current IARC carcinogenicity group listing was found for propylparaben/sodium propylparaben in the classification dataset checked.
A Taiwan population study reported paraben hazard indices below 1 in its probabilistic assessment.

populations: Children (higher food intake per kg body weight)
Male developmental windows (reproductive-endpoint concern in regulatory toxicology)
adi_exceedance.notes: For E217 specifically, current EFSA/JECFA positions do not provide an active positive ADI; conventional ADI exceedance quantification is therefore not robustly defined for this additive.

risk_assessment.rationale: Major-regulator signals converge toward elevated concern: EFSA excluded E217 from temporary ADI support, JECFA withdrew ADI for propylparaben due reproductive toxicity concerns, and EU authorization for E217 was removed.
key_factors: EFSA 2013: E217 not retained within temporary ADI framework
JECFA 2006: ADI withdrawn for propyl p-hydroxybenzoate
Recent mechanistic/animal studies continue to show toxicity signals
